```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Paths in the code are relative to the project root (folder with the .Rproj)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5,
                      fig.align = "center")
library(curatedTCGAData)        # curated TCGA data as MultiAssayExperiment objects
library(MultiAssayExperiment)   # container linking several omics to the same patients
library(TCGAutils)              # helpers for TCGA barcodes and sample types

# Helper: record the number of patients after each preparation step
flow <- data.frame(step = character(), patients = integer())
add_step <- function(flow, step, n) rbind(flow, data.frame(step = step, patients = n))
```

# Overview

This report documents the preparation of the **TCGA breast invasive carcinoma
(BRCA)** multi-omics data used in the project. It runs the same steps as
`01_data_preprocess/01_data_preparation.R`. Three omics layers are combined
with the clinical data:

- **RNA-seq**: RSEM gene-level counts (`RNASeq2Gene`), normalised to `log2(CPM + 1)`.
- **DNA methylation**: Illumina 450k array, beta values (`Methylation_methyl450`).
- **Protein**: reverse-phase protein array (`RPPAArray`).

**Steps:**

1. Download the data with `curatedTCGAData` (version 2.1.1).
2. Keep primary tumour samples from patients with data in all three omics.
3. Normalise the RNA-seq counts to `log2(CPM + 1)` (no features are filtered).
4. Harmonise sample and patient identifiers across datasets.
5. Select female patients with a known pathological stage and define a three-level
   stage outcome.
6. Split patients into a **training set (`r params$train_prop * 100`%)** and a
   **test set (`r (1 - params$train_prop) * 100`%)**, with the same split in every dataset.
7. Save (or compare with the saved) `.rds` files in `data/data_split/`.

**General principle:** every dataset contains **the same patients in the same
order**, and the split is done at **patient level** and **before any
data-driven preprocessing** (filtering, imputation, scaling). Every later QC
decision is made on the training set only and then applied to the test set.
The only transformation applied here, `log2(CPM + 1)`, is computed sample by
sample and therefore does not share information between training and test.

# Data download

## Available assays

With `dry.run = TRUE` the function only lists the assays available for BRCA,
without downloading anything.

```{r dry-run}
curatedTCGAData(diseaseCode = "BRCA", assays = "*",
                version = "2.1.1", dry.run = TRUE)
```

## Selected assays

| Assay | Content |
|---|---|
| `RNASeq2Gene` | RSEM gene-level counts (raw, non-negative) |
| `Methylation_methyl450` | DNA methylation, Illumina 450k array (beta values, 0–1) |
| `RPPAArray` | Protein expression, reverse-phase protein array (log2, median-centred) |

The result is a `MultiAssayExperiment` object; the clinical data are in
`colData()`. Downloads are cached by ExperimentHub, so later runs are fast.

```{r download}
brca <- curatedTCGAData(
  diseaseCode = "BRCA",
  assays      = c("RNASeq2Gene", "Methylation_methyl450", "RPPAArray"),
  version     = "2.1.1",
  dry.run     = FALSE
)

brca
names(experiments(brca))   # exact assay names used below

flow <- add_step(flow, "Downloaded (patients in colData)", nrow(colData(brca)))
```

# Sample selection

## Primary tumours with all three omics

`TCGAprimaryTumors()` uses the sample type code in the TCGA barcode
(e.g. `TCGA-A1-A0SB-01A-...`): it keeps `01` = primary solid tumour and removes
`06` = metastatic, `11` = solid tissue normal, etc. `intersectColumns()` keeps
only patients with data in all three omics.

```{r primary-tumours}
brca <- TCGAprimaryTumors(brca)
brca <- intersectColumns(brca)

lengths(colnames(brca))    # samples per assay (should be equal)

flow <- add_step(flow, "Primary tumour, all three omics", nrow(colData(brca)))
```

# Omics and clinical data

Each omics matrix has features in rows and samples in columns. The methylation
assay is stored on disk (HDF5) and is converted to an in-memory matrix
(~485,000 probes), which takes some time and memory.

```{r extract}
counts <- assay(brca[["BRCA_RNASeq2Gene-20160128"]])
meth   <- as.matrix(assay(brca[["BRCA_Methylation_methyl450-20160128"]]))  # HDF5 -> in-memory matrix
prot   <- assay(brca[["BRCA_RPPAArray-20160128"]])
clin   <- as.data.frame(colData(brca))                                     # one row per patient

data.frame(dataset = c("RNA-seq counts", "Methylation", "Protein", "Clinical"),
           rows    = c(nrow(counts), nrow(meth), nrow(prot), nrow(clin)),
           columns = c(ncol(counts), ncol(meth), ncol(prot), ncol(clin)),
           content = c("genes x samples", "CpG probes x samples",
                       "proteins x samples", "patients x variables"))
```

## RNA-seq: counts to log2(CPM + 1)

Raw counts should be non-negative and without missing values. RSEM expected
counts can contain some non-integer values, which is expected.

```{r rna-counts}
data.frame(check = c("Minimum value", "Maximum value", "Negative values",
                     "Missing values", "Proportion of integer values"),
           value = c(min(counts, na.rm = TRUE), max(counts, na.rm = TRUE),
                     sum(counts < 0, na.rm = TRUE), sum(is.na(counts)),
                     round(mean(counts == round(counts), na.rm = TRUE), 3)))
```

Counts per million (CPM) correct for sequencing depth using only each sample's
own total, so they can be computed before the split without leakage. The
`log2(x + 1)` transformation gives a scale from 0 to about 20, without negative
or missing values. **No genes are filtered at this step**: the filtering of
lowly expressed genes is learned later on the training set only.

```{r rna-cpm, fig.height = 4.5}
lib_size <- colSums(counts)                          # total counts per sample
rna      <- log2(t(t(counts) / lib_size * 1e6) + 1)  # log2(CPM + 1), genes x samples
rm(counts); invisible(gc())

data.frame(check = c("Minimum value", "Maximum value", "Negative values",
                     "Missing values", "Genes", "Samples"),
           value = c(round(min(rna), 2), round(max(rna), 2), sum(rna < 0),
                     sum(is.na(rna)), nrow(rna), ncol(rna)))

hist(lib_size / 1e6, breaks = 40, col = "grey70", border = "white",
     main = "Library size per sample", xlab = "Total counts (millions)")
```

The `sampleMap` links each omics sample (full barcode) to its patient.

```{r samplemap}
smap <- as.data.frame(sampleMap(brca))
head(smap)
```

# Identifier harmonisation

## Barcodes to patient IDs

The omics matrices use full sample barcodes (e.g. `TCGA-A1-A0SB-01A-11R-A144-07`),
while the clinical data use patient IDs (`TCGA-A1-A0SB`). `TCGAbarcode()`
trims the barcodes to the first 12 characters.

```{r trim-barcodes}
colnames(rna)  <- TCGAbarcode(colnames(rna))
colnames(meth) <- TCGAbarcode(colnames(meth))
colnames(prot) <- TCGAbarcode(colnames(prot))
```

## Duplicated patients

If a patient had more than one aliquot of the same tumour, only the first is kept.

```{r duplicates}
data.frame(dataset    = c("RNA-seq", "Methylation", "Protein"),
           duplicated = c(sum(duplicated(colnames(rna))),
                          sum(duplicated(colnames(meth))),
                          sum(duplicated(colnames(prot)))))

rna  <- rna[,  !duplicated(colnames(rna))]
meth <- meth[, !duplicated(colnames(meth))]
prot <- prot[, !duplicated(colnames(prot))]
```

# Clinical selection and outcome

## Female patients

Male breast cancer is rare and biologically different, so only female patients
are kept.

```{r female}
table(clin$gender, useNA = "ifany")

clin <- clin[which(clin$gender %in% "female"), ]

flow <- add_step(flow, "Female", nrow(clin))
```

## Known pathological stage

Patients with stage `"stage x"` (stage cannot be assessed) or a missing stage
are removed. Missing values are removed explicitly; otherwise they would be
assigned to the last category of the outcome below.

```{r stage-filter}
table(clin$pathologic_stage, useNA = "ifany")

clin <- clin[!is.na(clin$pathologic_stage) & !clin$pathologic_stage %in% "stage x", ]

flow <- add_step(flow, "Known pathological stage", nrow(clin))
```

## Outcome: pathological stage in three categories

| Outcome | Original stages |
|---|---|
| `stage i` | stage i, ia, ib |
| `stage ii` | stage ii, iia, iib |
| `stage iii` | stage iiia, iiib, iiic, iv |

Stage IV is grouped with stage III because it has very few patients.

```{r outcome}
clin$outcome_p.stage <- ifelse(clin$pathologic_stage %in% c("stage i", "stage ia", "stage ib"), "stage i",
                               ifelse(clin$pathologic_stage %in% c("stage ii", "stage iia", "stage iib"), "stage ii",
                                      "stage iii"))

# Each original stage must map to exactly one category
table(clin$pathologic_stage, clin$outcome_p.stage, useNA = "ifany")
```

# Alignment of omics and clinical data

Only patients present in all three omics and in the filtered clinical data are
kept, in the same order everywhere.

```{r align}
common <- Reduce(intersect, list(colnames(rna), colnames(meth),
                                 colnames(prot), rownames(clin)))

rna  <- rna[,  common]
meth <- meth[, common]
prot <- prot[, common]
clin <- clin[common, ]

flow <- add_step(flow, "Aligned across all datasets", length(common))

data.frame(check = c("RNA-seq columns = clinical rows",
                     "Methylation columns = clinical rows",
                     "Protein columns = clinical rows"),
           value = c(all(colnames(rna)  == rownames(clin)),
                     all(colnames(meth) == rownames(clin)),
                     all(colnames(prot) == rownames(clin))))
```

## Patients in rows

Machine learning functions expect patients in rows and features in columns.
`check.names = FALSE` keeps the original feature names (e.g. `HLA-A` would
otherwise become `HLA.A`). A `patientID` column is added to each dataset; it
is an identifier, not a predictor.

```{r transpose}
rna  <- data.frame(t(rna),  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
meth <- data.frame(t(meth), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
prot <- data.frame(t(prot), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

rna$patientID  <- rownames(rna)
meth$patientID <- rownames(meth)
prot$patientID <- rownames(prot)
```

# Train/test split

Patients are split at random into a training set and a test set. The seed is
set right before sampling, so the split is reproducible.

```{r split}
set.seed(params$seed)

train_ids <- sample(rownames(clin), size = round(params$train_prop * nrow(clin)))
test_ids  <- setdiff(rownames(clin), train_ids)

rna.train  <- rna[train_ids, ]
meth.train <- meth[train_ids, ]
prot.train <- prot[train_ids, ]
clin.train <- clin[train_ids, ]

rna.test   <- rna[test_ids, ]
meth.test  <- meth[test_ids, ]
prot.test  <- prot[test_ids, ]
clin.test  <- clin[test_ids, ]
```

## Sanity checks

No patient may appear in both sets, and the rows must be in the same order in
all the datasets of each set.

```{r split-checks}
data.frame(
  check = c("No overlap between training and test",
            "Training: RNA-seq = clinical", "Training: methylation = clinical",
            "Training: protein = clinical",
            "Test: RNA-seq = clinical", "Test: methylation = clinical",
            "Test: protein = clinical"),
  value = c(length(intersect(train_ids, test_ids)) == 0,
            all(rownames(rna.train)  == rownames(clin.train)),
            all(rownames(meth.train) == rownames(clin.train)),
            all(rownames(prot.train) == rownames(clin.train)),
            all(rownames(rna.test)   == rownames(clin.test)),
            all(rownames(meth.test)  == rownames(clin.test)),
            all(rownames(prot.test)  == rownames(clin.test)))
)
```

## Outcome distribution

The split is **not stratified**, so the proportion of each stage is checked in
both sets.

```{r outcome-props}
tab <- rbind(training = table(clin.train$outcome_p.stage),
             test     = table(clin.test$outcome_p.stage))
data.frame(set = rownames(tab), patients = rowSums(tab),
           round(prop.table(tab, 1), 3), check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
```

# Saved datasets

Each dataset is a separate `.rds` file in `data/data_split/`. By default
(`params$save = false`) this report does not overwrite them: it checks that the
patients and features it obtains are the same as in the saved files used by
the rest of the project.

```{r save}
path.x <- "./data/data_split"
objs <- list(rna.train  = rna.train,  meth.train = meth.train,
             prot.train = prot.train, clin.train = clin.train,
             rna.test   = rna.test,   meth.test  = meth.test,
             prot.test  = prot.test,  clin.test  = clin.test)

if (isTRUE(params$save)) {
  dir.create(path.x, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  for (nm in names(objs)) saveRDS(objs[[nm]], file = file.path(path.x, paste0(nm, ".rds")))
}

do.call(rbind, lapply(names(objs), function(nm) {
  file  <- file.path(path.x, paste0(nm, ".rds"))
  saved <- if (file.exists(file)) readRDS(file) else NULL
  data.frame(file     = paste0(nm, ".rds"),
             patients = nrow(objs[[nm]]),
             columns  = ncol(objs[[nm]]),
             same_patients_as_saved = !is.null(saved) && identical(rownames(saved), rownames(objs[[nm]])),
             same_columns_as_saved  = !is.null(saved) && identical(colnames(saved), colnames(objs[[nm]])))
}))
```

# Summary

```{r flow}
flow
```

1. **Three omics layers and clinical data** were downloaded from TCGA-BRCA and
   restricted to primary tumours from patients with data in all three omics.
2. **RNA-seq counts were normalised** to `log2(CPM + 1)`, without filtering any gene.
3. **Identifiers were harmonised** at patient level (`TCGA-XX-XXXX`).
4. **`r nrow(clin)` female patients with a known pathological stage** were kept,
   with a three-level outcome (stage i / ii / iii, stage iv grouped into iii).
5. Patients were split into **`r length(train_ids)` for training** and
   **`r length(test_ids)` for testing**, with the same split in every dataset and
   no overlap.

**Next step:** quality control of each omics layer on the training set
(`02_qc_*`).
